English (the core figure): 8 of the 93 local governments shown pay more for home-made computing and still pay for other computing; 4, Huangyan district, Taizhou; Ningbo city; Changsha Economic and Technological Development Zone; and Sichuan province, pay for home-made computing only; the other 81 state no higher rate for home-made computing: 80 pay one rate for all, and Hangzhou city pays 30% or 20% “by the type of computing facility” (按照算力设施的不同类型), a type its plan does not name (its rule of 2024, since repealed, paid 30% for home-made and 20% for other facilities). The rate shown is the one for an ordinary applicant; most rules state it as a ceiling (up to). What is counted is a rule that pays a share of a firm’s bill for rented or bought computing: most call the payment a computing voucher (算力券) or a like name; 38 give it another name, a subsidy, a reward or support, and are tagged or marked †. One row per government (a province, a city, a district or a zone): its latest general rule found that is in force and states a share of the bill. These are the rules found by searches that went province by province and city by city, saved and read, not a census of every local government: the searches covered the 31 province-level governments, 24 named cities and new areas, and the cities, districts and zones on the lists of four searches that went city by city; other districts and counties only as they turned up. 52 of the 93 are read on an official page or file of the issuing government or body, and 41 in another copy (another body’s site, a news or commercial site, or an Internet Archive capture). Left out: rules known only from the press or a summary (Yuhang district, Keqiao district and Jinan city among them), application guides (Beijing city’s economy bureau; Nanjing), plans with no date of effect (Nanjing’s Jiangbei New Area), rules repealed, expired or with no share of the bill (Longgang district of Shenzhen, and Nanchang city’s top-up of a provincial award, among them), rules whose text was not reached or only as a scan (Chongqing; Xihu district of Hangzhou), and drafts. Counted other ways (rules / paying more / home-made only / no higher rate): with Hangzhou city’s two tiers read as home-made and other, as its repealed rule had them, 93 / 9 / 4 / 80; with Hangzhou city left out, 92 / 8 / 4 / 80. Support for building or buying with home-made chips only is separate: Beijing city’s plan for 2024 to 2027 supports, by a share of the investment, “采购自主可控GPU芯片开展智能算力服务的企业” (firms that buy independently controllable GPU chips to provide computing services). Of the 8 rules that pay more, 7 word the favoured kind 自主 or 自主可控 (independent or independently controllable), and Binhai New Area’s rule says 自主信创 (independent Xinchuang).

Chinese: 英国《金融时报》（2026年11月13日）报道：国家网信办和国家安全部内部侧重安全的官员把对英伟达的依赖看作战略弱点（原文：“viewed dependence on Nvidia as a strategic vulnerability”），商务部倾向于进口（原文：“favoured imports”），据该报援引的未具名知情人士称，2025年晚些时候限制进口和使用性能较低的英伟达芯片的行动由国家发展改革委牵头（原文：“was led by the National Development and Reform Commission”）。美国贸易代表2026年11月20日说（彭博电视；机器字幕，未经人耳核对，01:06至01:35）：情况并不像人们让你以为的那样铁板一块（原文：“not as monolithic as people would have you believe”）；按他自己的分析（原文：“my own analysis”），有人想要获得美国芯片（原文：“we’d like to have access”），也有人认为反正不要美国芯片（原文：“others who think, well, we don’t want American chips anyway”）。两条字幕轨的断句不同，因此他是否把这一分歧放在政府内部，并无定论。

where: page: inside Beijing: note 2

Nvidia’s reports say the preliminary finding concerns the “degraded products” US export controls required it to offer the Chinese market. A standing rule cuts the other way: the regulator’s 2020 approval of Nvidia’s Mellanox purchase obliges Nvidia to keep supplying its accelerators to the Chinese market, unless lifted since (the parties may apply to lift the conditions six years after they took effect) (decision).
Chinese: 一篇介绍市场监管总局党组工作的未署名文章把英伟达案与高通公司、杜邦中国集团的案件一并列在“坚决落实党中央重大决策部署”和“敢于斗争”之下（共产党员手机报，2026年9月24日）。英伟达的报告说，初步调查结论涉及美国出口管制要求它向中国市场提供的降规产品（原文：“degraded products”）。有一项规定（如未解除）方向正相反：市场监管总局2020年附条件批准英伟达收购迈络思，条件之一是英伟达须“向中国市场继续供应英伟达GPU加速器”；交易双方可在条件生效6年后申请解除（公告全文）。

where: page: note 1

Chinese: 空心圆点依据的是未具名人士的说法。在找到的答复中，没有中国主管部门证实其中任何一条：被问到这类报道时，外交部发言人先后表示“我不了解你提到的情况”（2025年8月13日）、“具体问题建议向中方主管部门进行询问”（2026年1月29日）、“中方在美国输华芯片问题上的立场是一贯的”（2026年11月9日）。

where: page: note 2
English (the core figure): No published Chinese order against buying Nvidia chips was found in the policy pages and national document lists read. The published acts against Nvidia that were found were a summons and an antitrust case. Of 297 state and Party media items on Nvidia and its chips found from Jul 2025 to Nov 2026, 34 only warn. 23 date from Jul 31, 2025 to Sept 24, 2025. Of the 11 outside those weeks, one is dated Jul 24, 2025, one Nov 1, 2025, and 6 date from Dec 9, 2025 to Jan 14, 2026 in reports on the American easing for the H200. The last 3 are in Global Times in 2026. 14 items mix a warning with a welcome, 10 after September 2025. These warnings are not orders. The searches and the scan of saved pages yielded a sample of what the outlets printed.
Chinese: 在所阅读的政策网页和全国性文件目录中，没有找到公开发布的、不准购买英伟达芯片的中国政府命令。在所查资料中，找到的针对英伟达的公开举措有两项：一次约谈和一起反垄断案件。2025年7月至2026年11月间找到297篇涉及英伟达及其芯片的官方媒体和党媒内容，其中34篇只提出警示，23篇出自2025年7月31日至2025年9月24日。这八周之外还有11篇：2025年7月24日和2025年11月1日各一篇，2025年12月9日至2026年1月14日期间有6篇涉及美国放宽H200出口，最后3篇见于2026年《环球时报》英文版。另有14篇既有警示也有欢迎，其中10篇在2025年9月以后发表。这些警示都不是命令。检索和查阅存档网页得到的是样本。

where: page: note 3
English (the core figure): By subject, 219 of the later items concern chips for AI computing, including 33 that only warn. Another 40 concern products with an Nvidia chip. 8 concern Nvidia as a company, and 30 concern other subjects. A separate January 2024 to June 2025 sample holds 174 items, 160 from outlets covered by the later sample and 14 from three People’s Daily group papers outside it. One baseline item warns against reliance on the H20. None of the 160 comparable items was found to tell buyers not to buy Nvidia chips. Across both periods, 23 of the 35 warnings fall in those eight weeks. On Dec 3, 2024, the Internet Society of China called on companies to be careful in choosing to buy American chips, citing US export controls, and asked them to use chips made in China by domestic and foreign-funded firms alike.
Chinese: 按主题看，后期样本中219篇涉及AI算力芯片，其中33篇只提出警示。另有40篇涉及使用英伟达芯片的产品，8篇涉及英伟达公司，30篇涉及其他主题。2024年1月至2025年6月的另一组样本有174篇，其中160篇出自后期也覆盖的媒体，14篇出自不在后期样本中的三份人民日报社旗下报纸。前期有一篇警示不要过度依赖H20。在160篇可比文章中，没有找到要求买方不买英伟达芯片的内容。两期共找到35篇警示，其中23篇出自这八周。2024年12月3日，中国互联网协会以美国出口管制为由，呼吁企业“审慎选择采购美国芯片”，同时呼吁“积极使用内外资企业在华生产制造的芯片”。

where: page: note 4
English (the core figure): Some purchases were reported approved by outlets citing people they did not name. Nvidia’s own filings report licensed sales to China. The filings and other records cite American curbs as causes far more often than they cite Chinese acts.
Chinese: 一些媒体援引未具名人士报道，部分采购获得批准。英伟达自己的披露文件报告了获许可的对华销售。披露文件和其他记录把美国限制列为原因的次数，远多于把中国举措列为原因的次数。

where: page: note 5
English (the core figure): Records 4 and 16 are an antitrust case against Nvidia the company. By Nvidia’s own reports the preliminary finding concerns the degraded products that US export controls required it to offer the Chinese market. They are drawn orange as pressure on Nvidia, not as a wish for fewer Nvidia chips. The White House said on Nov 1, 2025 that China would end its investigations of US firms in the chip supply chain, naming none; neither the regulator’s own news list (read to Nov 23, 2026) nor Nvidia’s reports say the Nvidia case has ended, and the regulator’s review of its 2025 work, posted Apr 10, 2026, lists the further investigation.
Chinese: 第4条和第16条记录是针对英伟达公司本身的反垄断案件。按英伟达自己的报告，初步调查结论涉及美国出口管制要求其向中国市场提供的降规产品。这两条画成橙色，表示对英伟达的压力，并不表示希望英伟达芯片减少。白宫2025年11月1日说，中国将终止对芯片供应链上美国企业的各项调查，但没有点名；市场监管总局自己的新闻列表（读至2026年11月23日）和英伟达的报告都没有说英伟达案已经结束，总局2026年4月10日发布的2025年工作回顾仍列有“对英伟达公司实施进一步调查”。

where: page: note 6
English (the core figure): What Beijing meant is not settled. American bodies read its antitrust moves as leverage or pressure: the US-China commission (2025), “exert leverage and ease pressure as a negotiating tactic”; the Congressional Research Service (Sept 2025), “to pressure Nvidia to provide its advanced chips to China”. Yet asked whether China would let its companies buy the H200, the Trade Representative said “that’s gonna be a sovereign decision for China” (May 15, 2026, Bloomberg Television; captions, not checked by ear, at 05:59). Either reading leaves the direction of the acts drawn here as it is.
Chinese: 北京方面的用意并无定论。美国的一些机构把它的反垄断举措看作筹码或施压：美中经济与安全审查委员会（2025年）认为，这显示中国愿意把施加影响和缓解压力都用作谈判手段（原文：“exert leverage and ease pressure as a negotiating tactic”）；国会研究服务处（2025年9月）认为，这是为了向英伟达施压，要它向中国提供先进芯片（原文：“to pressure Nvidia to provide its advanced chips to China”）。不过，被问到中国是否会让本国企业购买H200时，美国贸易代表说，那将是中国的主权决定（原文：“that’s gonna be a sovereign decision for China”；2026年5月15日，彭博电视；字幕，未经人耳核对，05:59处）。无论取哪一种解读，这里所画各项举措的方向都不变。

where: page: note 7
English (the core figure): The H200 also had to pass American conditions: testing in the United States, shipments to China and Macau of no more than half of the same product shipped for end use in the United States, and a 25% tariff (Commerce Department rule of Jan 15, 2026; Nvidia’s report for the quarter ended Jul 26, 2026). By May 11, 2026 Washington had returned without action the applications for 1,888,950 of the 3,444,160 chips listed, more than half of that list (the bars above). The committee that released the table says the summary does not show every application in full; its example is an Nvidia application of Dec 19, 2025 for 445,000 chips for Tencent; the table’s only Tencent row of that date is for 75,000, approved, and neither document says whether it is that application.
Chinese: H200还须满足美方的条件：在美国境内检测、发往中国和澳门的数量不超过同一产品在美国供最终使用的发货量的一半、缴纳25%的关税（美国商务部2026年1月15日的规则；英伟达截至2026年7月26日季度的报告）。截至2026年5月11日，在表内所列申请涉及的3,444,160枚芯片中，华盛顿未予处理即退回的申请涉及1,888,950枚，超过该表所列的一半（见上方条形图）。公布这份表格的委员会说，这份汇总没有完整反映每一份申请；它举的例子是英伟达2025年12月19日为腾讯申请44.5万枚的一份申请；表中这一日期英伟达为腾讯所列的只有一行，为7.5万枚、已批准，两份文件都没有说这一行是否就是那份44.5万枚的申请。

where: page: note 8
English (the core figure): The chip at issue changed over time: the H20 (2024 to 2025), the RTX PRO 6000D (2025), the H200 (from December 2025), the RTX PRO 5500 (2026).
Chinese: 所涉芯片前后有变化：H20（2024年至2025年）、RTX PRO 6000D（2025年）、H200（2025年12月起）、RTX PRO 5500（2026年）。

where: page: note 9
English (the core figure): The records are a selection made to show both sides, not a census. The count of marks in a row is not a measure.
Chinese: 这些记录是为呈现双方情况而作的选取，不是全面统计。某一行圆点的多少不代表分量。

where: page: note 10
English (the core figure): Records 1 and 2 are not about Nvidia. Record 1 is the 2023 review conclusion that failed Micron’s products, a published instruction to operators of critical information infrastructure to stop buying one foreign chip maker’s products; record 2 is a purchase rule for the desktop computers of Party and state bodies and of the institutions directly under them or supporting them. They are drawn in orange as steps away from foreign chips. In record 30 the universities issued their own procurement notices and held suppliers to the government procurement law’s conditions. This was not an act of the central government. Records 35 and 37 do not name Nvidia. They are drawn blue because they back Chinese firms’ computing abroad. The Financial Times, citing two unnamed people on Nov 27, 2025, said firms were training abroad “to access Nvidia’s chips” (record 47). Records 42 and 55 are a city body’s and a Party journal’s documents about what the companies use; they are drawn in the companies’ row.
Chinese: 第1条和第2条记录与英伟达无关。第1条是2023年认定美光产品未通过审查的结论，是一项公开发布的、要求关键信息基础设施运营者停止采购一家外国芯片厂商产品的指示；第2条是针对党政机关及其直属或为其提供支持的事业单位台式计算机的采购规定。这两条画成橙色，表示远离外国芯片的举措。第30条是两所高校自行发布的采购公告，要求供应商符合政府采购法规定的条件。这不是中央政府的举措。第35条和第37条没有提到英伟达。它们画成蓝色，因为有关部门支持中国企业使用境外算力。英国《金融时报》2025年11月27日援引两名未具名人士报道，有企业在境外训练模型以使用英伟达芯片（原文：“to access Nvidia’s chips”，第47条）。第42条和第55条是一个市级部门和一份党刊关于企业用什么芯片的文件；它们画在企业一栏。
